summary: Horace Geoffrey Quaritch Wales (1900–1981) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Charterhouse School and Queens' College, Cambridge (~1919–1922), he served as Field Director for the Greater India Research Committee (~1934–1941).

Indologist Horace Hayman Wilson (1786–1860) served as Assay Master at the Kolkata Mint (1816–1833) and Boden Professor of Sanscrit at Oxford (1833–1836). He was also an East India Company librarian and Director of the Royal Asiatic Society (1837).

Horace L. Friess (1900–1975) was a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied at Columbia University (~1915–1926) and Heidelberg University. He held posts at Johns Hopkins University and Columbia University, where he was attested as professor in 1970.

Horst Lasic is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who earned his PhD from the University of Vienna in 1999. He worked as a research fellow at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (1995) and taught Tibetan and Sanskrit at Vienna (1999).
Hoseok Leigh works in philosophy and religious studies. He studied under teacher Ha-u Kim and earned a Doctor of Philosophy from the California Institute of Integral Studies, attested in 2010.
Hoshu Mitsuhara (1916–2004) was a Buddhist studies scholar who served on the faculty at Koyasan University, where he was attested as professor in 1982 and emeritus professor in 2004.
Houn Jiyu-Kennett (1924–1996) was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at Durham University and under traditional teachers Sek Kim Seng (~1962) and Keidō Chisan Kohō (~1962–1963).

Hoyo Watanabe (born 1933) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (~1952–1960). He spent his career at Rissho University as a professor of Buddhist studies (~1974–2003) and served as dean of the faculty (attested 1984–1985).
Hozen Seki (1903–1991) was a Buddhist studies figure who founded the American Buddhist Academy and served as resident minister at the New York Buddhist Church (attested 1998).

Hsiang-Kuang Chou was a sinology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Swami Sivananda. He held posts at Delhi, Allahabad (attested 1960), the Lal Bahadur Shastri National Academy (attested 1960), and was Chancellor of Yoga-Vedanta Forest Academy (attested 1960).

Hsiao-Lan Hu works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. Hu earned a PhD from Temple University and served as associate professor of Religious Studies and Women's and Gender Studies at the University of Detroit Mercy (attested 2017).

Hsing Yun (1927–2023) worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Yin Shun and at the University of Hong Kong, founded Fo Guang Shan and University of the West, and held a post at National Taiwan University.
Hsiu-hui Ji is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed an MA at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin, attested in 2009.

Hsu-feng Lee specializes in Buddhist studies. Lee earned a master's degree under Huimin at the Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies and a PhD under Mark Allon at the University of Sydney, attested in 2017.

Hsuan Hua (1918–1995) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Hsu Yun in 1948. He founded Dharma Realm Buddhist University, the Buddhist Text Translation Society, and the Institute for World Religions, and was Abbot of the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas (~1976–1995).
Hsueh-li Cheng (1939–2020) was a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. Cheng held academic posts at Ohio University and at the University of Hawaii at Hilo (~1977–2017).

Hu Shih (1891–1962) was a scholar of philosophy, sinology, and history/archaeology. Educated at Cornell and Columbia (PhD 1915–1917), he held posts at Peking University (professor 1946), Fu Jen Catholic University, and Academia Sinica (president 1958).

Huai-Chin Nan (1918–2012) worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and sinology. He studied at the Republic of China Military Academy and under teacher Huanxian Yuan (~1942–1945), later serving as Professor of Philosophy at Chinese Culture University (attested 1986).

Huaiyu Chen (born 1974) specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. He earned a master's at Peking University under Xinjiang Rong (1994), completed doctoral studies under Stephen F. Teiser, and was assistant professor at Arizona State University (~2007–2013).

Huanhuan He works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He has held positions at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, the University of Tokyo (attested 2015), and Zhejiang University as a professor (attested 2015).
